shots.title: CrewPot · Solana Hackathon
shots.narration: Meet CrewPot. Shared money, with rules your crew agrees on. Let’s walk through a real Solana Devnet example, using test tokens with no real monetary value.

shots.title: A prepared pot. A fixed agreement.
shots.narration: Let’s take a weekend gaming fund. Three friends put in ten demo USDC each. The pot needs two approvals before paying out. The recipient and deadline are fixed from the start, so everyone knows the agreement.

shots.title: Member 1 contributes
shots.narration: First, one friend puts in ten. You can see their share in the vault.

shots.title: Member 2 contributes
shots.narration: Another friend joins in. The pot now holds twenty, confirmed on Solana.

shots.title: Fully funded. Still awaiting approval.
shots.narration: The last ten brings us to thirty. But the money still can’t leave.

shots.title: One approval. Payout stays locked.
shots.narration: One member approves. That’s one vote out of two. The money stays locked.

shots.title: The majority authorizes the payout
shots.narration: Now the second member approves. That’s the majority. The payout is authorized, and anyone can finalize it, but only to the recipient the crew agreed on.

shots.title: 30 dUSDC released to the agreed recipient
shots.narration: The payout is complete. All thirty demo USDC reached the agreed recipient, and the vault is empty. Behind the scenes, our script checks the exact balance change. These activity links open the real, confirmed transactions on Solana Explorer.

shots.title: Plans changed. Your share is yours.
shots.narration: If plans fall through, contributors have a way out. In this separate pot, the deadline passed without enough funding or approval. The friend who put in ten claims that ten back, without needing the organizer’s permission. The member now shows refunded, and the vault is empty.

shots.title: Your crew. Your money. Your rules.
shots.narration: CrewPot. Your crew. Your money. Your rules.
